flow.definition: A quantity that accrues per period and accumulates over time (e.g. units sold in a period).

stock.definition: A level read at a point in time; it does not accumulate over time (e.g. inventory on hand).
stock.time: not foldable (resolve the stored row, or refuse)

intensive.definition: A per-entity magnitude that is meaningful only as an average, never a total (e.g. a duration, an age, a rate, a ratio, or a signed deviation). Summing it across a population double-counts or is meaningless; the correct fold on ANY axis is a mean / median / percentile, not a SUM.

precomputed.definition: A measure whose value EXISTS ONLY at the grains it was computed for — you locate the row matching the requested axis/parameter combination and read it. Nothing is derivable from narrower cells: the source documentation describes one such reach measure as non-additive (a sum or average of the measure is not the measure of the summed or averaged inputs) and computed iteratively. v0.1.15: `precomputed` is a property of the MEASURE, not of an axis — every axis of such a measure is simply `none`, because no fold is valid anywhere. Where the value comes from is a measure_type fact; whether you may fold is an axis fact.
precomputed.time: not foldable (resolve the stored row, or refuse)
precomputed.categorical: not foldable (resolve the stored row, or refuse)

target.definition: A planning target, not an observed quantity (e.g. a sales goal); not summable on any axis.
target.time: not foldable (resolve the stored row, or refuse)
target.categorical: not foldable (resolve the stored row, or refuse)

measure_concepts.name: Discount
measure_concepts.definition: Σ Quantity × (UnitPrice − NetPrice). The account is knowledge/discount.md.

measure_concepts.name: ExchangeRate
measure_concepts.label: Exchange Rate
measure_concepts.definition: What one currency was worth in another on one day: 100,450 quoted rates over a date and an ordered pair of currencies. The account is knowledge/exchange_rate.md.

measure_concepts.name: GrossRevenue
measure_concepts.label: Gross Revenue
measure_concepts.definition: What Contoso would have charged at list: quantity times the undiscounted price, per sale, summed. The account is knowledge/gross_revenue.md.

measure_concepts.name: Margin
measure_concepts.label: Margin (gross profit)
measure_concepts.definition: Σ Quantity × (NetPrice − UnitCost), identical to Revenue − COGS. The account is knowledge/margin.md.

measure_concepts.name: NetRevenue
measure_concepts.label: Net Revenue
measure_concepts.definition: What Contoso actually charged: quantity times the discounted price, per sale, summed. The account is knowledge/net_revenue.md.

measure_concepts.name: SalesCost
measure_concepts.label: Sales Cost
measure_concepts.definition: What the goods on a sale cost Contoso: quantity times unit cost, per sale, summed. The account is knowledge/sales_cost.md.

measure_concepts.name: UnitsSold
measure_concepts.label: Units Sold
measure_concepts.definition: How many items went out: the quantity on a sale, summed. The account is knowledge/units_sold.md.

dimensions.name: Brand
dimensions.definition: Whose name a product is sold under: eleven names, carried as a column on the product row with no table and no key of their own. The account is knowledge/brand.md.

dimensions.name: Color
dimensions.label: Colour
dimensions.definition: The colour a product comes in: sixteen values on the served row, and the one attribute that on its own makes a new SKU — "E400 Green" and "E400 Orange" are two products. The account is knowledge/color.md.

dimensions.name: Country
dimensions.definition: A country Contoso sells in — 8 of them, plus one `--` sentinel that is not a place. The account is knowledge/country.md.

dimensions.name: Currency
dimensions.definition: The money a sale is denominated in: five ISO codes, pointed at by every sale and by both ends of every exchange rate. The account is knowledge/currency.md.

dimensions.name: Customer
dimensions.definition: A person on Contoso's customer register: 104,990 of them, each with a name, a birth date and a place — continent, country, state, city. HALF HAVE NEVER ORDERED: 52,189 of the 104,990 appear on a sale, so the register is not the buyer list. The account is knowledge/customer.md.

dimensions.name: Location
dimensions.definition:
THE PLACE a store stands on — a country and a state, and nothing that belongs to the shop itself. Floor area, opening and closing dates are properties of PREMISES and live on Store; what a place owns is where it is.
ONE PLACE MAY HOLD A SUCCESSION OF PREMISES over time, which is the fact this concept exists to keep separate from Store: `dim_store.store_key` declares `finer_than: location_code`, so premises roll UP into a place and a place never divides down into one. Summing a per-premises measure over a place that has been re-let counts it once per tenancy.
A PLACE IS NOT A CITY IN THIS BUNDLE. Its finest geography is `state`, which in France means regions and overseas territories; `main.store` carries no city or town column. City exists only on the customer, as where a customer lives, and is declared personally identifying.
No counts here, by the ruling of 2026-10-24 — they belong in data/profiles/dim_location.yaml where they can be re-measured. The account is knowledge/location.md.

dimensions.name: Order
dimensions.definition: One customer's purchase on one date, counted by distinct `order_key` over the line relation. The account is knowledge/order.md.

dimensions.name: Product
dimensions.definition: A thing Contoso sells, at the level the shelf knows it: a SKU. The account is knowledge/product.md.

dimensions.name: ProductCategory
dimensions.label: Product Category
dimensions.definition: How Contoso groups what it sells: eight categories, each over several of thirty-two sub-categories, both carried as names on the product row. The account is knowledge/product_category.md.

dimensions.name: Store
dimensions.definition:
THE PREMISES Contoso sells from — a shop that stood on one place for one trading period, with its own name, floor area, opening date and closing date. It is what every sale is recorded against.
A PLACE MAY HOLD A SUCCESSION OF PREMISES, so a store is NOT its place: see the Location concept for the place, and `dim_store.store_key#rulings.finer_than` for the declaration that one rolls up into the other. The account is knowledge/store.md.
THIS DEFINITION CARRIES NO COUNTS, by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-24: "you are disclosing values that variy through the time as constnts?!?!?! this is no go ... you can decribe things without constants too". It used to say how many stores there were and how many were trading, which was a measurement of one day frozen into a sentence — and it disagreed with this concept's own `counts:` key, which is how one word came to name two grains. Counts belong where they can be re-measured: data/profiles/dim_store.yaml.
